title: The cartesian open comparison on varying-ring systems relabels lifts
statement:
Let $R_n$ be arbitrary commutative rings with maps $\varphi_n:R_{n+1}\to R_n$, and use the ordinary semilinear module-system categories $\mathscr S_X$ on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with exact inverse image $f^*_\bullet$ and open extension by zero $j_{!,\bullet}$ of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]. Let $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $p:W\to T$ be a morphism of schemes, put $W'=W\times_TS$ with projections $b:W'\hookrightarrow W$ and $q:W'\to S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $\beta:p^*_\bullet i_{!,\bullet}\to b_{!,\bullet}q^*_\bullet$ be the inverse of the open-adjunction transpose of inverse-image composition after the open unit, as in [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows]. Then for every $N\in\mathscr S_S$ and every $n$:

(1) the underlying abelian sheaf of $(p^*_\bullet N')_n$, for any system $N'$ on $T$, is the abelian inverse image $p^{-1}N'_n$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] with the induced $(R_n)_W$-action; the underlying abelian sheaf of $(i_{!,\bullet}N)_n$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the direct-sum presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], whose local sections over an object $U\to T$ are finite sums $[c,x]$ of a lift $c:U\to S$ of $U\to T$ through $i$ and a section $x\in N_n(U\xrightarrow{c}S)$; similarly for $b_{!,\bullet}$ with lifts through $b$. Under these identifications the semilinear transitions of $p^*_\bullet i_{!,\bullet}N$ and of $b_{!,\bullet}q^*_\bullet N$ send $[c,x]$ to $[c,t_n(x)]$, where $t_n:N_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}N_n$ is the transition of $N$.

(2) $\beta_n$ sends a local section $[c,x]$, pulled back along $h:H\to W$ with $c$ a lift of $p\circ h$ through $i$, to the section $[(h,c),x]$ labelled by the induced lift $(h,c):H\to W'$ of $h$ through $b$; the inverse sends a lift $a$ through $b$ to $q\circ a$. Consequently $\beta$ is an isomorphism of ordinary systems, natural in $N$, commuting with the semilinear transitions. No flatness, finiteness or noetherian hypothesis on the $R_n$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] to the geometric morphism of small pro-etale topoi in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], separately with each constant ring $R_n$. It identifies the underlying abelian inverse image and its unit with the module inverse image and its unit, and identifies $f^{-1}(R_n)_T$ with $(R_n)_X$ by the same constant scalars. These identifications also respect $\varphi_n$: both scalar maps send a constant $r$ to the constant $\varphi_n(r)$. Hence applying abelian inverse image to the transition of a system gives its semilinear transition after pullback. The simultaneous levelwise inverse image of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] is left adjoint to the sectionwise system direct image: the level adjunction bijections carry the equations expressing compatibility with transitions to one another, by naturality of the units. The left-adjoint specification in [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] therefore identifies this functor with $f^*_\bullet$, with these units. This proves the inverse-image assertion in (1), for arbitrary $N'$ on $T$.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, (2), (5), (6); applying fixed-ring scalar endomorphisms levelwise

proof.text: For $j=i$ or $b$, the ordinary open localization in [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] is the module extension of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Thus $(j_{!,\bullet}M)_n=P_{M_n}^{\#}$, with $P$ exactly as in [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification of this direct-sum presheaf. The explicit adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint], applied after forgetting scalars, sends a map $v:M_n\to j^*F$ to the map $[c,x]\mapsto v_{(U,c)}(x)$. Taking the transpose of the identity of $j_!M_n$ therefore gives the open unit $x\mapsto[\mathrm{id},x]$ on the localized site. This map is linear by the summandwise scalar action in $P$, so the same formula is the module unit. This proves the extension assertion of (1) and fixes the unit normalization needed below.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, statement and proof: presheaf formula and the explicit adjunction

proof.text: By [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], applying a module map to $P$ acts only on its section coordinate. For the semilinear map $t_n$, give the target the $R_{n+1}$-action via $\varphi_n$; then $[c,x]\mapsto[c,t_n(x)]$ is additive and satisfies $[c,t_n(rx)]=[c,\varphi_n(r)t_n(x)]$. It commutes with restriction because $t_n$ does. Sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] consequently gives the system transition of $j_!M$. Step 1 says inverse image applies to the same map and leaves the pulled-back lift label fixed. Consequently both $A=p^*_\bullet i_{!,\bullet}N$ and $B=b_{!,\bullet}q^*_\bullet N$ have the transition formula in (1). Here, on the inverse-image side, $x$ denotes a pulled-back local representative; no expression $N_n(H\to S)$ is used unless $H\to S$ is an object of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, summandwise functoriality; agent semilinear calculation

proof.text: For any $h:H\to W$, the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] gives mutually inverse functions $c\mapsto(h,c)$ and $a\mapsto q\circ a$ between lifts of $p\circ h$ through $i$ and lifts of $h$ through $b$. Indeed $b(h,c)=h$, $q(h,c)=c$, and $(ba,qa)=a$ by uniqueness. For $v:H'\to H$ the same uniqueness gives $(h,c)v=(hv,cv)$. Thus the relabelling respects restrictions, and it does not alter the section or its scalar action.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, lift indices; agent fibre-product universal-property calculation

proof.text: Write $\delta=\beta^{-1}:B\to A$. By [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows], its transpose is $q^*N\xrightarrow{q^*\eta_i}q^*i^*i_!N\xrightarrow{\chi}b^*p^*i_!N$, where $\chi$ is the specified inverse-image composition comparison. Step 2 computes $\eta_i$ as insertion into the lift-labelled summand. The normalization in [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] and the unit/composition compatibility of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] mean that $\chi$ identifies the two pullbacks of that same section along $iqa= pba$. On a localized object $(H,a)$ with $ba=h$, this transpose therefore sends $x$ to the pulled-back section $[qa,x]$. Applying the explicit extension adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint] now gives $\delta_n([a,x])=[qa,x]$. This computes the specified arrow, rather than choosing a separate base-change isomorphism. All occurrences of $x$ after pullback mean the image of a section under the inverse-image unit (and its restrictions); the formula also applies additively to their local representatives.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, explicit adjunction; agent calculation for the unit-defined comparison

proof.text: For $a=(h,c)$, Step 4 gives $qa=c$. Step 5 reads $\delta_n([(h,c),x])=[c,x]$. Since $\beta$ is the inverse of this specified invertible transpose [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows], applying $\beta_n$ gives exactly $\beta_n([c,x])=[(h,c),x]$. Conversely its inverse sends $[a,x]$ to $[qa,x]$. These formulas respect restrictions by Step 4 and finite sums by additivity. For a system map $u:N\to M$, both orders, applying $u$ and relabelling, send $[a,x]$ to $[qa,u_n(x)]$ on the direct-sum presheaf of $b_!q^*N$. The uniqueness in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] extends this equality to sheaves. Hence $\delta$, and therefore its inverse $\beta$, is natural in $N$.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, summand formula; agent inversion and naturality calculation

proof.text: Let $T^A_n,T^B_n$ denote the underlying abelian transition maps of $A,B$. On a generator $[a,x]$ of the extension presheaf of $B_{n+1}$, Steps 3 and 5 give $T^A_n\delta_{n+1}[a,x]=[qa,t_n(x)]=\delta_nT^B_n[a,x]$. The equality holds for arbitrary sections $x$ of $q^*N_{n+1}$: the transition of $q^*N$ is the inverse image of $t_n$, as established in Step 1. Both maps are additive and semilinear over $\varphi_n$, so the presheaf equality extends uniquely to its sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Multiplying by $\beta_n$ on the left and $\beta_{n+1}$ on the right yields $\beta_nT^A_n=T^B_n\beta_{n+1}$. Thus the computed level maps and their inverses are maps of ordinary systems. This establishes (2) with the stated transition compatibility. The proof used arbitrary fixed-ring inverse image and summandwise semilinearity, so requires none of the excluded coefficient hypotheses.
